scenes.text: PINPOINT. Blueprints that show their work.

A site engineer loses hours every day hunting through drawing sets for one number. General A.I. reads a drawing like a photo, and guesses. PINPOINT reads the geometry inside the file, and every answer comes with a receipt. Graded the way Stoa grades: counts exact, quantities within two percent.

Let's ask, in German: how many W.C.s are on this plan? Four. Each one is boxed and numbered on the real sheet, and it matches the ground truth exactly. The receipt says how: a bowl with no drain circle is a W.C., cited to the D.X.F. layer and its position on the sheet.

Now an area takeoff. The net floor area of apartment A: eighty point three three square metres, against a reference of eighty point three four. Within zero point zero one percent. All nine rooms are shaded, and each one is checked against its own printed label.

PINPOINT also catches errors in the drawings themselves. On this U.S. sports complex, the door schedule lists forty-one doors, but the plans tag only thirty-nine. Door one-eighteen C has no tag anywhere. That's an R.F.I. before the supplier orders frames off the wrong list.
An Estonian office floor, asked in Estonian. Forty-two doors, exact. Pick door three, and the sheet and the B.I.M. model fly to the same door, by its I.F.C. GlobalId.
Any 2D plan becomes a building you can walk through, with the counted W.C.s glowing. Brief your crew before they ever set foot on site.
One click gives the whole floor's bill of quantities: rooms, net areas, doors, windows and sanitary fixtures. Every line traced to the drawing, and ready to export as C.S.V. or P.D.F.

And the cost. The same seven thousand, seven hundred and forty-one graded questions. A frontier vision model: about a hundred and seventy euros, at list price. PINPOINT: less than a quarter of a cent, measured. About seventy-two thousand times cheaper, with zero L.L.M. calls in the scored path.
Every source is scored on its own, never blended. Swiss C.A.D. plans and I.F.C. models: one hundred percent. Finnish raster scans: seventy-three percent, with every miss left visible.
PINPOINT. Every answer comes with a receipt.
